posts.title: Suomi.fi keeps HSTS for only a week.
posts.text:

posts.title: INP: how fast the page answers a tap.
posts.text:
Word of the day: INP: how fast the page answers a tap.

Interaction to Next Paint measures the delay from a click, tap or key press to the next frame on screen. It replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024.

Spot it: Find the slowest tap on your page, often a menu or a filter, and break up the long task behind it.

posts.title: SRI: a fingerprint for borrowed scripts.
posts.text:
Word of the day: SRI: a fingerprint for borrowed scripts.

Subresource Integrity puts a hash of the file in the tag. If the CDN ever serves anything else, the browser refuses to run it.

Spot it: List the scripts you load from other domains. Add an integrity hash to every one that has a fixed version.

posts.title: Myth: the padlock means the site is secure.

HTTPS encrypts the trip between the browser and the server. It says nothing about the page's scripts, headers and cookies, or about who is behind the site.

Check it: Check what the padlock does not cover: response headers, cookie flags, outdated scripts and a DMARC record.

posts.title: Myth: a Lighthouse 100 means accessible.
posts.text:

posts.title: This week in web quality.
posts.text:
This week in web quality, Oct 30, 2026

Five picks from our daily sweep of the field, each summed up in our own words and credited to its source.

1. W3C maps the web for AI agents
W3C's Strategy Team set out how the web's technical agenda should change now that AI agents act on people's behalf, while keeping people at the center of the web. The paper goes to the Web and AI Interest Group at TPAC on Oct 29, and W3C is asking for feedback.
By Philippe Le Hegaret, W3C: https://www.w3.org/news/2026/w3c-and-the-state-of-the-web-in-the-ai-era/

2. axe-core 4.14 turns on Label in Name
Axe-core 4.14.0 now runs the WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name rule by default. It flags any control whose accessible name does not contain its visible label, like a Home button named Start page, which voice control users may not be able to click by saying Home. Deque tested the built-in voice control on macOS, iOS, Android and Windows before turning the rule on.
By Wilco Fiers, Deque: https://www.deque.com/blog/find-label-in-name-issues-in-every-scan-with-axe-core-4-14-0/

3. Screen reader tests in Playwright
Craig Morten shows how Guidepup lets a Playwright test drive a real screen reader and assert on what…

posts.title: Put the mouse away. Can you reach everything?
posts.text:

posts.title: The slowest page is rarely the home page.
posts.text:
Teams tune the home page and forget the pages people reach from search. Measure every page you link to, in the order a visitor would open them.

Try this today: List your five most visited pages from analytics and time each one. Fix the slowest first.

How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=tips-2026-10&utm_content=slowest-page

posts.title: The missing CSP: anything can crawl in.
posts.text:
Without a Content-Security-Policy header, the browser runs any script that ends up in your page, including one an attacker injected.

Exorcise it today: Check your response headers for Content-Security-Policy. Start in report-only mode, read the reports, then enforce it.

How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=horror-headers-2026-10&utm_content=missing-csp

#Halloween #CyberSecurity #Vulnerability #QA #CSP #QAlab
posts.alt: Horror headers, Security card. The missing CSP: anything can crawl in. No CSP (fail): HTTP/2 200, content-type: text/html. With CSP (pass): content-security-policy:,   default-src 'self';,   object-src 'none'.
